facts.fact: In 1991 India's forex reserves covered only about two to three weeks of imports (about US$1.2 billion).
India pledged gold to raise foreign exchange in 1991.
The Gulf War pushed up oil prices and cut remittances, triggering the crisis.
India did not default on its external debt in 1991.
The LPG reforms were launched by PM P.V. Narasimha Rao and FM Manmohan Singh.
Stabilisation measures are short-term macro corrections; structural reforms are long-term efficiency changes.
Globalisation shifted India from import substitution to export promotion and global integration.
The 1991 reforms abolished industrial licensing for most industries.
The MRTP Act was amended in 1991 and later replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.
Sectors earlier reserved for the public sector were de-reserved.
A Department of Disinvestment was created in 1999; BALCO and VSNL were early strategic sales.
SEBI was established as the capital-market regulator in 1992.
The Narasimham Committee guided banking reforms such as cuts in SLR/CRR and Basel norms.
Trade reforms cut tariffs, removed quantitative restrictions and created SEZs.
The BoP records all transactions between residents and the rest of the world on a double-entry basis and always balances.
The current account records merchandise trade, services, income and unilateral transfers.
The capital account covers capital transfers such as debt forgiveness and non-produced assets like patents.
The financial account records FDI, portfolio investment and reserve assets.
The rupee has been current-account convertible since August 1994; capital-account convertibility is only partial.
The Tarapore Committees (1997, 2006) gave the capital-account convertibility roadmap.
An "errors and omissions" entry reconciles BoP data gaps.
FDI gives control over management/assets; FPI does not.
FEMA, 1999 (replacing FERA 1973) governs foreign exchange; DPIIT frames FDI policy; FIPB was abolished in 2017.
FDI enters by the automatic route or the government (approval) route.
Defence allows 74% FDI automatic; telecom and single-brand retail 100%.
Insurance FDI cap was raised to 100% in December 2025 (74% from 2021).
Net FDI fell from about US$42 bn in FY23 to US$26.5 bn in FY24 (Economic Survey 2023-24).
The WTO began on 1 January 1995, replacing the GATT.
MFN requires a trade advantage given to one member to be extended to all members.
TRIPS = intellectual property; TRIMS = investment measures; GATS = services; SPS = food safety.
The Peace Clause (Bali 2013) protects India's public food stockholding and MSP from challenge.
National Treatment requires imported and domestic goods to be treated equally once in the market.
Agreement on Agriculture, SPS measures and Peace Clause all relate to the WTO (UPSC 2015).
FTP 2023 came into effect on 1 April 2023 under the DGFT, has no end date and targets US$2 trillion exports by 2030.
CEPA = UAE (May 2022), ECTA = Australia (Dec 2022), TEPA = EFTA (Oct 2025), CETA = UK (Jul 2026).
India–EFTA TEPA carries a US$100 billion investment pledge over 15 years.
India withdrew from RCEP in 2019.
The IMF bailout in 1991 was about US$2.2 billion (source text).
The rupee was devalued in two steps on 1 and 3 July 1991.
The New Industrial Policy was announced on 24 July 1991.
LERMS (a dual exchange rate) came in March 1992 and a unified market rate in March 1993.
NEP objectives: cut inflation, rebuild forex reserves, raise growth, enlarge the private sector, integrate with world markets.
The Malhotra Committee recommended opening insurance, leading to the IRDA Act, 1999.
The C. Rangarajan Committee (1993) dealt with disinvestment.
Narasimham Committees were set up in 1991 and 1998.
The Department of Disinvestment was renamed DIPAM in 2016.
New Telecom Policy came in 1999 and TRAI in 1997.
The Electricity Act came in 2003 and UDAY (for DISCOMs) in 2015.
RTE Act 2009 and Ayushman Bharat 2018 are listed as social-sector reforms.
AMRUT (2015), Bharatmala, NHDP and Smart Cities are infrastructure reforms.
Code on Wages 2019; Industrial Relations and Social Security Codes 2020.
Aadhaar 2010, BharatNet 2011, Jan Dhan 2014 and Digital India 2015 are digital reforms.
UPI was launched in 2016 and ONDC in 2022.
The National Cyber Security Policy dates from 2013.
National Digital Communications Policy came in 2018; 5G roll-out followed in 2022-23.
After 1991 export share, FDI and forex reserves rose; agriculture's share in GDP fell (UPSC 2017).
Post-1991, IT and services boomed while agriculture saw reduced public investment.
The AP Electricity Reform Act 1998 unbundled APSEB into APGENCO and APTRANSCO (1999) with APERC as regulator.
The World Bank-assisted Andhra Pradesh Economic Restructuring Project began in 1998.
AP's Vision 2020 (1999) was the Chandrababu Naidu government's long-term plan; today it is Swarna Andhra @2047.
Current account includes balance of trade and invisibles; foreign assets and SDRs are not (UPSC 2014).
Capital account includes foreign loans, FDI and portfolio investment; private remittances are current (UPSC 2013).
India: merchandise exports < imports; services exports > imports; overall CAD (UPSC 2020).
IT export earnings and remittances reduce currency-crisis risk; government spending does not (UPSC 2019).
India is the world's largest recipient of remittances.
With exports $500 bn, imports $700 bn, FDI $100 bn and remittances $50 bn, the current account deficit is $150 bn.
BoP-crisis consequences: currency depreciation, inflation, unemployment and dependence on bailouts.
Devaluation is a deliberate cut in a fixed rate; depreciation is a market-driven fall.
A rise in NEER means rupee appreciation; REER is NEER adjusted for inflation.
Convertibility means freely converting the rupee into other currencies and vice versa (UPSC 2015).
Forex reserves = foreign currency assets + gold + SDRs + Reserve Tranche Position.
India's forex reserves first crossed US$700 billion in September 2024.
Participatory Notes let overseas investors invest without registering with SEBI (UPSC 2019).
Masala bonds are rupee-denominated bonds issued abroad, first by the IFC.
ECB is External Commercial Borrowing by Indian firms.
An FPI holding of 10% or more in a company is treated as FDI.
GIFT City IFSC (Gujarat) is regulated by the IFSCA (2020).
FDI brings technology and management and is stable; FII adds general capital and is volatile (UPSC 2011).
AP is India's largest farmed-shrimp producer, so exchange rates and US tariffs hit AP farm incomes.
GATT was signed in 1947 with India among its 23 founding contracting parties.
The Uruguay Round (1986-94) led to the Marrakesh Agreement of 15 April 1994.
WTO DG Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (since 2021) is the first woman and first African DG.
The WTO has 166 members and is headquartered in Geneva.
The 1st Ministerial (Singapore 1996) gave the "Singapore issues".
The Doha Development Round was launched at Doha in 2001.
Nairobi (2015) agreed to end farm export subsidies.
MC12 at Geneva (2022) agreed on fisheries subsidies.
MC13 was at Abu Dhabi (2024) and MC14 at Yaoundé, Cameroon (2026).
Amber box = trade-distorting, capped; blue box = production-limiting, allowed; green box = minimal distortion, allowed (UPSC 2016).
The de minimis limit is 10% for developing and 5% for developed countries.
The TFA was part of the Bali package (2013), ratified by India and in force from February 2017 (UPSC 2017).
TRIMS covers trade in goods only and bans quantitative import restrictions on foreign investors; it does not regulate foreign investment (UPSC 2020).
India amended the Patents Act 1970 in 2005 to allow product patents under TRIPS.
Section 3(d) of the Patents Act blocks evergreening (Novartis case, 2013).
India's first compulsory licence was granted to Natco for Bayer's Nexavar (2012).
The WTO Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019.
The Chinese renminbi was added to the IMF SDR basket in 2016 (UPSC 2016).
The IMF and IBRD were born at Bretton Woods in 1944.
World Bank Group: IBRD 1944, IDA 1960, IFC 1956, MIGA 1988, ICSID 1966.
Ease of Doing Business was published by the World Bank (UPSC 2016), discontinued in 2021 and replaced by B-READY.
The Global Competitiveness Report is published by the World Economic Forum (UPSC 2019).
UNCTAD (1964) publishes the World Investment Report.
AIIB (2016, Beijing): China largest, India second-largest shareholder; has non-Asian members (UPSC 2019).
NDB (BRICS, 2015) is in Shanghai; its first president was K.V. Kamath.
India's WTO defence of public stockholding protects paddy-procuring States like AP.
The India–EU FTA was concluded on 27 January 2026 and called the "mother of all trade deals".
The India–EU deal was earlier negotiated as the BTIA (UPSC 2017).
India–Oman CEPA was signed on 18 December 2025 and came into force on 1 June 2026.
India–New Zealand FTA was signed on 27 April 2026 and enters into force on 20 October 2026.
India–UK CETA was signed on 24 July 2025 at Chequers and came into force on 15 July 2026.
India–EFTA TEPA was signed on 10 March 2024 and came into force on 1 October 2025.
SAFTA came into force in 2006 and the India–Sri Lanka FTA in 2000.
The Singapore CECA (2005) was India's first CECA.
ASEAN–India trade in goods agreement came into force in 2010.
India–South Korea CEPA came into force in 2010 and India–Japan CEPA in 2011.
India–Mauritius CECPA (2021) was India's first trade deal with an African country.
APTA (Bangkok Agreement, 1975) is India's oldest regional trade agreement.
India walked out of RCEP in November 2019 over Chinese imports and dairy.
Trade deals with the USA, Canada, Israel, Peru and South Africa are under negotiation.
RoDTEP (January 2021) replaced MEIS for export tax refunds.
EPCG allows duty-free capital goods against an export obligation.
FTP 2023 raised the courier e-commerce export limit from ₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh.
FTP 2023 promotes Districts as Export Hubs and Towns of Export Excellence.
Kandla (1965) was Asia's first Export Processing Zone.
Visakhapatnam EPZ (Duvvada) is one of the original central EPZs, now Visakhapatnam SEZ.
SEZ Policy came in April 2000 and the SEZ Act in 2005; the EOU scheme dates from 1981.
Sri City in Tirupati district is a large private multi-product SEZ.
From 27 August 2025 most Indian goods faced a 50% US tariff, including a 25% penalty for Russian oil.
The 25% Russian-oil penalty tariff was withdrawn in February 2026.
The 50% US tariff hit Andhra Pradesh shrimp farmers hardest among States.
The Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025 raised insurance FDI to 100%.
Digital news media allows 26% FDI with government approval.
E-commerce marketplace model allows 100% FDI; the inventory model is not allowed.
Renewable energy allows 100% FDI under the automatic route.
Press Note 3 (April 2020) requires government approval for FDI from land-border countries.
SEBI (FPI) Regulations, 2019 merged FIIs, sub-accounts and QFIs into FPIs.
The source text lists three FPI categories (I: governments/central banks; II: funds/banks; III: others).
Global FDI fell 2% to US$1.3 trillion in 2023 (UNCTAD).
India's FDI plus portfolio inflows have averaged about 2.5% of GDP a year (IMF).
Digital FDI share rose from 46.6% (FY17) to 69.2% (FY21).
Top FDI sources are Singapore, Mauritius and the USA.
Net FDI shrank in 2024-25 because of repatriation and outward FDI.
Make in India was launched in 2014.
The National Single Window System gives investors one-stop clearances.
DMIC and the Chennai–Bengaluru corridor are industrial corridors used to attract FDI; VCIC passes through AP.
